eng.name: LEGEND
eng.title: LEGEND: the body
eng.role: Builds, poses and moves the people in a film: their skeleton and proportions, their hands, what their joints can do, how they hold and move things, and how well they move.
eng.intro: Every version is the whole body done to full precision; each adds what LEGEND had to learn to do more with it.

levels.title: Anatomy
levels.focus: Every joint inside the range a human joint has; mass and balance like a body's.

facts: Shoulder: flexion to 180, extension 50 to 60, across the body about 50
Elbow: to about 145 (a few degrees of hyperextension); forearm: pronation about 80, supination 80 to 90
Wrist: flexion 60 to 80, extension 60 to 70, radial 20, ulnar 20 to 30
Fingers: knuckle 90, middle joint 100 to 110, last joint 70 to 90 (about two thirds of the middle one); thumb knuckle 50 to 60, last joint 80
Hip: flexion 120 (more with the knee bent), extension 30, abduction 40 to 45 (more as the hip flexes), adduction 20 to 30
Knee to 135 to 150; ankle: dorsiflexion 20 (about 40 to 45 under the body's weight in a lunge), plantarflexion 50
Neck: flexion 50 to 60, extension 75, side bend 45, rotation 80; back: flexion 45 to 80, rotation 30 to 45
src: AAOS, Joint Motion: Method of Measuring and Recording
Soucie et al. 2011, Range of motion measurements: reference values
Hallaceli et al. 2014, Normal hip, knee and ankle range of motion

levels.title: Handling things
levels.focus: Holding everyday things the way people do, and the movements round them: reaching, lifting, handing over, throwing.

facts: Feix et al. (2016): 33 grasps in power, intermediate and precision classes, by opposition (palm, pad, side) and the thumb's position
Things over about 5 cm or 350 g are held in power grasps about 89% of the time (Feix, Bullock and Dollar 2014)

facts: Jeannerod (1984): a transport and a grip channel, coordinated
The hand's speed is one bell, peaking at about 40 to 45% of the reach (the landing is longer)
The grip opens wider than the thing, widest at 60 to 77% of the reach: about 55 mm plus 0.75 of its width (Smeets and Brenner 1999)

levels.title: The lens
levels.focus: What the camera really records: depth of field, motion blur from the shutter, natural vignetting.

studied.topic: Depth of field in a render
facts: Each pixel's blur circle from the thin lens: c = A f |d - s| / (d (s - f)), converted to pixels by the sensor's height
Scatter as gather: each pixel collects the light of the neighbours whose blur discs reach it, each spread evenly over its disc, light added in linear values
A sharp thing in front must hide what is behind it; a blurred thing in front spills over (Jimenez 2014, Next generation post processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare)
src: Jimenez 2014, Next generation post processing (SIGGRAPH course)

facts: The shutter is open for (angle / 360) of a frame: the streak is that share of the frame's motion
Camera motion blur by reprojecting each pixel's depth into the previous frame (Rosado 2007, GPU Gems 3 ch. 27)
Natural vignetting falls as cos^4 of the angle off the lens's axis
src: Rosado 2007, Motion blur as a post-processing effect (GPU Gems 3)

levels.title: Spacing and contact
levels.focus: The measure kept, blows arriving where and when they should, partners reacting on the beat, and the stage-combat gap.

facts: Measure: the distance at which a blow can reach; fighters work at it and step in or out
A staged blow that "lands" passes a hand's breadth (about 10 cm) beside the target, the gap hidden along the audience's or the lens's line
The reaction (head snap, fold) is the partner's job, timed to the moment of contact
src: Kreng 2008, Fight Directing: A Practical Guide

can: Fighters at measure, feet planted except when a step lifts them
Every blow on its target at its moment (or on the block that meets it), every reaction on the beat and in the blow's direction
The safety gap kept and hidden from the camera

levels.title: Phrases and rhythm
levels.focus: Moves joined into phrases with the pause-burst-pause rhythm, and several attackers who take their turns.

facts: Bordwell: the Hong Kong fight is built of pause, burst, pause; a burst's blows come fast, then a held moment
Jackie Chan's rules include rhythm (a beat to every phrase) and showing each hit fully
src: Every Frame a Painting 2014, Jackie Chan: How to do action comedy

facts: On screen the attackers take turns: only one engages at a time while the others stay out of reach (stacking)
The hero turns to face each one as they come
src: Every Frame a Painting 2015, The Bourne fights

levels.title: Reading on camera
levels.focus: Every exchange staged for the lens: hits that read, silhouettes that read, the hit and its reaction in one shot.

facts: The gap of a staged hit is hidden along the lens: the camera square to the strike's line sees the gap edge-on only from the wrong side
Show the hit and the reaction in the same shot (Jackie Chan); a blow reads when the limb crosses the frame in profile
Wide enough to see the bodies, still enough to read the move (the Bourne critique: cutting too fast loses the geography)
src: Every Frame a Painting 2014, Jackie Chan: How to do action comedy

eng.name: BOARD
eng.title: BOARD: the storyboard artist
eng.role: Reads a written scene, plans its shots, draws the board and the floor plan, keeps continuity, takes notes, and stages the scene for the other engines.
eng.intro: A new engine: from a page of prose to a board a crew could shoot from.

levels.title: Reading a scene
levels.focus: From prose to beats: the heading, the people, what each does, to whom, with what, and how.

facts: The scene heading: INT. or EXT., the place, the time of day
Action lines in the present tense; dialogue under the speaker; a character's name in capitals when they first appear
A beat is a unit of action or feeling: what changes
src: StudioBinder: how to write a scene heading

facts: Pronouns go back to the person they name (he, she, him, her); a description ("a stranger") is a person until named
A defence ("she ducks") answers the blow before it
Adverbs carry the manner (slowly, angrily), which Laban's efforts can play
src: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing: coreference

can: Scene headings, weather and light; the people (named, described, pronouns); walking, running, picking up, putting down, handing over, throwing, drinking, talking, looking, reacting, every blow and defence of a fight

levels.title: Panels
levels.focus: Each shot drawn from MIMATIC's camera with the people as LEGEND performs them, and the arrows a board uses.

facts: Frame lines at the film's aspect; the figures where the camera sees them
Arrows: a figure's movement inside the frame; the camera's move outside or on the frame (push in: arrows into the corners; pan or track: an arrow across; crane: up or down)

levels.title: Style, revisions and the animatic
levels.focus: A pencil look, a director's notes taken without disturbing the rest, and the board timed to the cut.

facts: Pencil: line weight falls with distance; hatching on the shadow side gives the light
